summary.tpReason: Telemetry directly confirms successful GCP account creation, RSA key creation, project-owner IAM grant, token-creator grant, permissive firewall, GPU miner instances, sensitive object reads, and logging-sink tampering by mirage from one IP. The sequence is clearly unauthorized persistence and abuse, not a benign deployment.
summary.fpReason: No telemetry supports an approved deployment; requested names include backdoor-svc-gcp and crypto-miner, and the actions include disabling/deleting logging and accessing confidential data.
summary.whatHappened: On 2026-08-19 from 17:49:10 to 18:01:05 UTC, mirage@pkwork.onmicrosoft.com, calling from 198.51.100.42 with a Windows browser user agent, operated in GCP project pocaas-prod-01. It created backdoor-svc-gcp@pocaas-prod-01.iam.gserviceaccount.com, created key abc123def456, granted that account roles/owner, and granted mirage serviceAccountTokenCreator on deploy-pipeline. The same identity opened allow-all-ingress (all protocols from 0.0.0.0/0), created crypto-miner-01 and crypto-miner-02 using a2-highgpu-8g, listed/read financial-report-2026.xlsx, employee-pii-export.csv, and api-keys-production.json, deleted export-all-logs, and disabled the _Default logging sink. Additional GCP activity shows crypto-miner-03 and other resource operations. A phishing email was delivered to mirage at 17:00:15 UTC; the corresponding sign-in query could not be evaluated because the table lacked TimeGenerated.

researchDone: Retrieved GCPAuditLogs schema and investigated the alert window plus surrounding activity for mirage and project pocaas-prod-01.
